name: veterinary_clinic_system_094_idempotent_daily_log_close
instruction:
Close out the boarding day, idempotently. For every boarding_reservation with status='checked_in', ensure there is a boarding_daily_log row for the episode date (log_date date prefix == episode date). If missing, create it with fed_am/fed_pm/medicated/walked all false, notes 'auto-closed ', logged_by 'system'. If a row already exists for that reservation and episode date, leave it completely unchanged. After closing, create or update exactly one ops_reports row {report: 'boarding_daily_close', batch_code, checked_in: , closed: , preexisting:

} where C is the count of checked_in reservations, N is the number of new log rows created this run, and P is the number that already existed. Running twice must create zero new log rows and update the same report row.
_max_steps_note: set after live gold measurement in QC session
_par_steps_note: set after live gold measurement in QC session

success_criteria.summary: One boarding_daily_log row for the episode date per checked_in reservation; pre-existing seed log rows byte-identical; new rows have exact fields; exactly one ops_reports boarding_daily_close row for this batch with checked_in, closed in {0, expected_new}, and preexisting matching the seed count for this episode; checked_in count validated by API and SQL.

checks.expect: One log row per checked_in reservation on episode date; seed logs untouched; one report row upserted by batch_code
checked_in count and expected new log count agree between API and SQL

hazards: The 5 checked_in boarding_reservations (ids 1-5) span check_in/check_out dates all before the episode date (2026-09-27..2026-10-03). The seed boarding_daily_log has 10 rows for reservations 1-5 on 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-04 (e.g., id 2 reservation 1 log_date 2026-09-04; id 4 reservation 2 log_date 2026-09-04). A solution that uses the build date or a fixed date instead of the episode date will find these older rows and either skip creating the required new rows or update them and break the seed canary.
There are 43 'reserved' and 92 'checked_out' boarding_reservations; a solution must not create daily log rows for reservations that are not checked_in.

The natural key for a daily log is (reservation_id, log_date). A blind insert for every checked_in reservation without checking for an existing row for the episode date will create duplicates on rerun.
The ops_reports boarding_daily_close row must be upserted by batch_code; a solution that pushes a new report row on every run will create duplicates.
Episode-date comparison must use the 10-char date prefix because log_date values are stored as full ISO timestamps (e.g., '2026-09-30T00:00:00.000Z').

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Scales a simple daily log close to 140 reservations with an existence-checked insert keyed by reservation+episode date, idempotent re-run, and an aggregate report. The verifier dual-path counts checked_in reservations and enforces that pre-existing seed logs for different dates are untouched.
